findings.title: Case-sensitive email matching allows bypassing blocked emails
findings.body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` queries `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` and `BlockedEmail` stores `email` without normalizing case. Because `User` does not downcase `email` before validation runs during `UsersController#create`, a user can bypass a blocked address (e.g. `bad@spam.com`) simply by signing up with mixed case (e.g. `Bad@spam.com`). `BlockedEmail` should normalize `email` to lowercase before saving and in `should_block?`.

findings.title: `BlockedEmail.match_count` is incremented multiple times per signup attempt
findings.body: `User` runs `EmailValidator`, which calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?` and increments `match_count` on every validation call. In `UsersController#create` (lines 168 and 172), `user.valid?` is called when `SiteSetting.call_discourse_hub?` is enabled, followed immediately by `user.save` (which runs validations again). Even when `valid?` is false or when `save` runs, a single signup or validation pass can increment `match_count` multiple times, and calling `user.valid?` as a read-only check has the side effect of mutating the database.

findings.title: Changing email bypasses `EmailValidator` and `BlockedEmail` checks
findings.body: `UsersController#change_email` creates an `EmailToken` for `lower_email` without running `EmailValidator` (or validating `User#email` until confirmation, and `EmailToken.confirm` updates the user's email). If `EmailToken` does not validate `email: true`, a user can sign up with an allowed email and then change their email to a blocked or domain-blacklisted address.
